label: FAQ — accordion
markup:
Questions

Before you ask

Does it work with my theme?

Yes. Lumen reads widths and colours from your theme first, and only overrides what you change.

What happens if I deactivate it?

Your content stays. The blocks fall back to their saved markup, so pages keep rendering.

Can I limit what editors can change?

Yes. The role manager can hide the styling tabs and leave only the content fields.

Is there a page builder to learn?

No. Everything happens in the block editor you already use.

label: FAQ — two columns
markup:
Support

Common questions

How do updates work?

Through the normal plugin updater. Block markup stays backwards compatible across major versions.

Is there a multisite licence?

Network activation counts as one site on Agency plans.

Can I export my design system?

Yes, as JSON, and import it into another site.

Do you offer refunds?

Thirty days, no questions, including on lifetime licences.

label: FAQ — on night
markup:
Answers

The ones people actually ask

Will this slow my site down?

Only the CSS a page uses is written into it, so an unused block costs a reader nothing.

Does it work with page caching?

Yes. Everything renders to static markup at save time.

What about accessibility?

Motion respects reduced-motion, and every interactive block ships with roles and labels.

label: FAQ — with a way out
markup:

Read these first

Where do I set global colours?

Lumen → Design System. Everything on the site follows what you set there.

Why is my block wider than the page?

Check the Columns block content width. Lumen reads it from your theme by default.

label: Content — two columns
markup:
Why another block plugin

Because most of them solve the first afternoon and none of them solve the second year. The controls that matter are the ones still legible when somebody else opens the site.

What we left out

No shortcodes, no proprietary storage, no lock-in on deactivate. Everything saves as standard block markup, which is the only real guarantee a plugin can offer.

label: Highlighted notice
markup:
One thing to set before you publish

Point the design library at your own endpoint, or keep using the patterns that ship with the plugin.

Read the setup note

label: Long copy with read more
markup:
The honest version

Most block plugins are judged on the day they are installed. That is the wrong day to judge one.

Read the rest

The day that matters is eighteen months later, when somebody who has never met you opens the site to change a phone number. If that person can find the setting, the plugin worked. If they file a ticket, it did not — however good the first afternoon felt. Every control in Lumen is built for that second person: named plainly, grouped where you would look, and resettable one value at a time.

Show less

label: Content — pull quote
markup:
On restraint

A block library is judged on what it refuses to add. Every control that ships is one more thing the next person has to understand before they can change a heading.

The best feature we shipped last year was the one we removed.
